_comment: Host profiles for R/00_paths.R (issue #29). Adding a machine is a stanza here,
not an edit to R code.
1. per-key env  ATLAS_<KEY>_DIR   e.g. ATLAS_WORKING_DIR, ATLAS_INDICES_DIR
2. root env     ATLAS_COMMON_DATA, then COMMON_DATA (shared with hazards_upstream);
ATLAS_HOST=<id> forces a profile regardless of detection
RULE: every host except cglabs pins BOTH trees to the same working_dir.
The nexgddp/atlas_delta fork only ever applied inside the CGlabs branch of the
old chain; letting the defaults template apply elsewhere would move the data
out from under every non-CGlabs checkout.

hosts.description: CGIAR JupyterHub / Kubernetes container. The only host that forks working_dir on climdat_source, and the only one carrying the monthly index trees.

capabilities.notes: No swap. Hard OOM ceiling - a stage that overcommits is killed, not slowed, which is why at least one stage is pinned to a single worker here. Source: server-environment-cglabs.md (on develop).

hosts.description: Afrilabs / PASCAL VM. Roughly 4x the cores and 2x the per-core clock of CGlabs, so the preferred target for CPU-bound stages once data is staged.

notes: NPROC LIES INSIDE JUPYTERHUB. A hub session runs in a systemd cgroup capped by the spawn profile (Small 8 vCPU/32 GB, Medium 16/64, Large 20/96), but nproc still reports 80 and affinity still shows 0-79. Anything calling detectCores() will oversubscribe by up to 10x. Check the real limit with: cat /sys/fs/cgroup$(cut -d: -f3 /proc/self/cgroup)/cpu.max - a first value of 800000 against a period of 100000 means 8 CPUs.
RStudio Server and plain SSH are NOT capped; those are the routes to the full 80 cores and 397 GiB.

No batch scheduler (no Slurm, no PBS) and ~69 accounts, so nothing stops one job saturating the machine. Sharing is by convention: pick a worker count deliberately, check uptime first, and export OMP_NUM_THREADS/OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS/MKL_NUM_THREADS.
No GPU and no CUDA. A sibling host 'ampere' may be GPU-equipped but is unconfirmed and needs separate IT access.
R's terra and sf link against the old system GDAL 3.4.3 / PROJ 8.2.1, while the python env carries GDAL 3.13.3. Relevant to COG and Zarr work.
Bulk store is roughly a quarter of CGlabs' free space, so a full mirror is not viable - stage per-shard working sets.
Source: server-environment.md, issue #27, branch docs/server-environment (NOT yet merged to develop). Figures taken from the live machine, September 2025, and will drift.

_unverified: PATHS are unverified; the CAPABILITIES above come from the documented note (issue #27).
working_dir and common_data are carried verbatim from the old R/0_server_setup.R:135 and have NOT been confirmed on the node.

Two descriptions disagree: /cluster01 is documented as holding Data, Projects and Workspace trees, while the working note refers to common_space/Workspace/common (shared data) and common_space/Workspace/atlas (Atlas tree).
Resolve with DISPATCH_pascal_issue29_profile.md, then correct common_data and both trees here and flip status to verified. No R changes needed.

hosts.description: Development laptop. Holds a partial staged copy of the setup-downloadable inputs, which makes it a usable second host for cross-host equivalence checks.

capabilities.notes: No monthly index trees. Suitable for the 0.4.x exposure chain and for resolver tests, not for R/1-R/3.

hosts.description: Windows checkout on D:. Carried over from the old chain; not known to be in current use.
Windows checkout on C:. Note the common_data root sits under C:/rprojects, not at the drive root - this asymmetry is inherited, not a typo.
